admission.justification: The current new large-list regression guards explicit nonpairing above the cell rail. Future callers must not reintroduce unbounded global alignment or infer a semantic pair from matching position; this would misattribute wording changes while removing a real resource boundary.

applicability: alignLists and gapRows over supplied ordered string lists, before presentation.
conditions: The initial whole-list product check is against DIFF_CELL_LIMIT; above it all items remain removed/added without pairing, even at matching positions.
Within budget, exact-text LCS and one-to-one moved pairs precede pairing equal-size remaining gaps.
Unpairable outputs retain their supplied strings/indices and a cell_limit or unpaired_gap reason.
exclusions: A bound on total output size, every allocation, whole-view latency or installed rendering; semantic equivalence of paired text; fresh test/browser execution.

evidence: dashboard/src/panels/review/wordDiff.test.ts::bounds list alignment without guessing pairs even for matching positions
dashboard/src/panels/review/wordDiff.test.ts::pairs a gap with equal counts for a word diff, and never pairs unequal gaps
Read exact whole-list and gap guards, moved pairing, prepared-passages and renderer note consumers. No input-wide runtime budget or semantic equivalence is inferred.

statement: Intent list alignment never invents a pair when its whole-list cell budget or remaining gap cardinality does not support one: over-budget lists and unequal remaining gaps retain ordered removed/added items with an explicit cell_limit or unpaired_gap reason.
